root_motivation: Grounding: a 2026-09-28 external security report registered arbitrary client_name/redirect_uris via mcphost's open DCR endpoint unauthenticated and confirmed the server persists and renders them verbatim -- the consent page today shows only client_name, so a self-registered app named "mcphost Official" renders indistinguishably from a verified one and the redirect destination is never shown. Real-world exploitability is low only because mcphost has ~0 real tenants (memory: self_mcphost_tenants_real_is_synthetic); the gap is structural and grows with every real user added. This PRD closes it with informed consent (a caution + destination host), not by gating DCR (a friction analysis showed gating adds real onboarding cost for little added security given redirect_uri is already per-client-bound).
user_persona: The mcphost end user approving a consent screen for an app they may not recognize, who wants to know whether it is self-registered and where their access is going before approving; the mcphost operator, who can mark a known client_id verified so first-party/vetted DCR clients aren't warned against; and the security reviewer responding to the 2026-09-28 report, who needs a consent screen that surfaces provenance and destination as the mitigation.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a DCR client (method="dcr") not operator-verified, When its /oauth/authorize consent page renders, Then it carries an unverified-application caution stating the app self-registered and is not verified by mcphost.
Given a CIMD client (method="cimd"), When its consent page renders, Then no unverified-application caution is rendered.
Given a consent page for any third-party client, When it renders, Then it displays the destination host of the redirect_uri the code would be delivered to.

Given a DCR client whose client_name is attacker-supplied (e.g. "mcphost Official" or HTML), When the consent page renders, Then the name is HTML-escaped and presented as self-asserted, never verified/first-party styled.

Given a DCR client registered with no client_name, When the consent page renders, Then it shows a neutral placeholder and still renders the caution and destination host, with no crash or empty-name injection.
Given a client_id on the operator verified-client allowlist, When its consent page renders, Then the unverified caution is suppressed even though method="dcr".
Given the unverified caution renders, When the user reads it, Then it links to a short explainer of what an unverified app means.
Given a user approves consent for an unverified (DCR, non-allowlisted) client, When the consent is recorded, Then the audit record notes the client was unverified at approval time.

Given an existing CIMD or first-party (allowlisted) consent flow, When a user completes it, Then behavior is unchanged -- consent still cannot be skipped, scopes still render -- and the caution is purely additive.

scope: src/authz.rs: render_consent_page now takes the resolving ClientIdentity plus the operator's VerifiedClientIds allowlist (state.verified_client_ids) instead of a bare client_name -- a DCR client not on the allowlist renders an unverified-application caution linking to a new short explainer, and every consent page (DCR or CIMD) shows the redirect_uri's destination host. display_client_name falls back to a neutral placeholder for a nameless client. post_authorize's existing 'consent' audit row now carries reason "unverified_client_at_approval" for an unverified approval, None unchanged otherwise.

src/state.rs: VerifiedClientIds -- a startup-parsed $MCPHOST_VERIFIED_CLIENT_IDS comma-separated list, same convention as the existing FleetIps/$MCPHOST_FLEET_IPS -- the PRD's own open-question default since no existing operator config surface is a global (not per-tenant) verified-client signal.
src/http.rs: new GET /oauth/unverified-app static explainer route.
src/claim.rs: a .caution/.self-asserted CSS addition to the shared consent-page STYLE constant.

tests/common/mod.rs: AppState gains verified_client_ids everywhere it's constructed; TestServer::start_with_verified_client_ids lets a test set the allowlist directly, same pattern as start_with_signup_rate_limit_and_fleet_ips.
non_goals: Gating or blocking DCR registration (no Initial Access Token, no CIMD-required mode, no global redirect allowlist) -- PRD's own Non-goals; open DCR stays open.
Changing rate-limiting or per-client redirect binding -- both already exist and are unchanged.

A client-approval/allowlist-to-connect workflow -- that's the separate mcphost-oauth-client-policy component; this PRD only suppresses the warning for an allowlisted client_id, it does not decide who may connect.
Measuring user behavior change (efficacy of the warning) -- the AC scope is that the correct UI renders for the correct client class.

additional.test_file_names_use_underscores_not_the_: The coder dispatch's own naming convention names test files after the literal (hyphenated) PRD slug, but scripts/gen-test-suites.sh's per-file consolidation declares `#[path = "<stem>.rs"] mod <stem>;` using the bare filename stem as a Rust identifier -- a hyphen there is a syntax error. Resolved by using the PRD slug with hyphens replaced by underscores (mcphost_oauth_unverified_client_consent_warning) as the test_prefix, the same shape every other test file in this repo already uses (docsqa, oauthpol, hostedas, ...).
additional.verified_client_allowlist_is_a_new_env_l: oauth_policy::OauthPolicy.allowlist (host.oauth.policy_set) already exists but is a per-TENANT connect/deny decision ("which clients may reach my consent screen at all"), not an operator-wide verification signal -- reusing it would mean every tenant has to independently allowlist mcphost's own first-party client_ids, and a client absent from one tenant's list would wrongly render as unverified even if the operator vouches for it globally. Resolved per the PRD's own open-question default: a new static, startup-parsed $MCPHOST_VERIFIED_CLIENT_IDS list, operator-wide.

five_whys_trace.q: Why warn instead of gating DCR registration outright?
five_whys_trace.a: PRD's own Non-goals: a 2026-09-28 friction analysis showed gating adds real friction to zero-touch MCP client onboarding for little added security, since redirect_uri is already per-client-bound (redirect_uri_allowed) -- this PRD is the friction-free alternative: informed consent, zero new steps.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is a CIMD client exempt from the caution but a DCR client is not?
five_whys_trace.a: Technical considerations: a CIMD client_id is a URL whose metadata document must fetch and validate (identify_client's is_cimd_client_id + cimd_cache.resolve) -- the client demonstrably controls a domain, a materially stronger provenance signal than an anonymous dcr_<random> id with no such proof.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the allowlist suppress the caution rather than reclassify the client as CIMD-equivalent?
five_whys_trace.a: Non-goals: this PRD only suppresses the warning for an allowlisted client_id, it does not decide who may connect -- that gating capability is the separate mcphost-oauth-client-policy component, so the allowlist stays a display-only exemption, not a trust upgrade with other side effects.

five_whys_trace.q: Why record 'unverified at approval time' on the audit row instead of deriving it later from the client's current method/allowlist state?
five_whys_trace.a: Open questions (default: record it, surfacing waits): the client's verification state can change after approval (added to or removed from the allowlist later) -- recording it at the moment of approval preserves what the user actually saw when they consented, which a later re-derivation from current state could no longer reconstruct.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does an operator config surface for a verified-client allowlist already exist to reuse, or is a new static list acceptable for P1?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No existing surface fits a global (not per-tenant) verified-client signal -- oauth_policy's own allowlist is per-tenant connect/deny. Per the PRD's own default: a new $MCPHOST_VERIFIED_CLIENT_IDS static list, read once at startup, same convention as the existing $MCPHOST_FLEET_IPS.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should the destination host show the full redirect_uri on hover/expand, or host-only always?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Per the PRD's own default: host-only. The PRD's own open question flagged 'full on expand' as a possible future enhancement but did not make it an AC, so this dispatch renders host-only with no expand affordance -- adding one would be scope beyond the listed ACs.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should P2's unverified-at-approval flag surface in the existing auth audit export now, or wait for mcphost-oauth-client-policy?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Per the PRD's own default: record it now (the existing host.oauth.audit/audit_export tools already surface every audit row's reason field verbatim, so no new surfacing code was needed), but no new dedicated summary/report for it -- that waits for mcphost-oauth-client-policy.
